Title:
 Quantitative Inorganic Analysis of Nitrite in 
 Raw Material

This document outlines 
 the testing procedures P1,which must be performed every 
 month M1 as indicated in the above title block and according to the Directives 
 of the Central Chemical Laboratories.
This analysis covers the determination of nitrite ion in water.

Nitrites react in warm acid solution (ca. 40C ) with permanganate solution in 
accordance with the equation :

If a solution of a nitrite is titrated in the ordinary way with potassium 
permanganate, poor results are obtained, because the nitrite solution has first 
to be acidified with dilute sulfuric acid. Nitrous acid is liberated, which 
being volatile and unstable, is partially lost. If, however, a measured volume 
of standard potassium permanganate solution, acidified with dilute sulfuric 
acid, is treated with the nitrite solution, added from a burette, until the 
permanganate is just decolorised, results accurate to 0.5-1 per cent may be 
obtained. This is due to the fact that nitrous acid does not react 
instantaneously with the permanganate.

More accurate results may be secured by adding the nitrite to an acidified 
solution in which permanganate is present in excess ( the tip of the 
pipette containing the nitrite solution should be below the surface of the 
liquid during the addition ), and back titrating the potassium permanganate with 
a solution of ferrous ammonium sulphate which has recently been compared with 
the permanganate solution.

For practice in this determination, it may be determine the purity of commercial 
potassium nitrite.

Pipets- Since this analysis depends on the amount of KMnO4 
consumed, it is imperative that pipets for delivering the potassium permanganate 
standard solution be calibrated and cleaned for maximum precision.

Weigh out accurately about 1.1 g. of 
commercial potassium nitrite, dissolve it in cold water, and dilute to 250 
ml. in a volumetric flask. Shake well.

Measure out 5 ml. of standard 0.1N-potassium permanganate into a 100-ml. flask, add 2.26 ml. conc. sulfuric 
acid, and heat to 40C.

Place the nitrite solution in the burette, and add 
it slowly and with constant stirring until the permanganate solution is just 
decolorised, better results are attained by allowing the tip of the burette to 
dip under the surface of the diluted permanganate solution.

Towards the end of the reaction is sluggish, so 
that the nitrite solution must be added very slowly.

Repeat the titration with two other 25 ml. portions 
of the permanganate solution.

Title:
 Quantitative Inorganic Analysis of Nitrite in 
 Raw Material
Introduction
This document outlines 
 the testing procedures P1,which must be performed every 
 month M1 as indicated in the above title block and according to the Directives 
 of the Central Chemical Laboratories.
This analysis covers the determination of nitrite ion in water.
Significance of Analysis
Nitrites react in warm acid solution (ca. 40C ) with permanganate solution in 
accordance with the equation :
2MnO4- + 5NO2- + 6H + 
 → 2Mn++ + 5NO3- + 3H2O
Summary of Analysis
If a solution of a nitrite is titrated in the ordinary way with potassium 
permanganate, poor results are obtained, because the nitrite solution has first 
to be acidified with dilute sulfuric acid. Nitrous acid is liberated, which 
being volatile and unstable, is partially lost. If, however, a measured volume 
of standard potassium permanganate solution, acidified with dilute sulfuric 
acid, is treated with the nitrite solution, added from a burette, until the 
permanganate is just decolorised, results accurate to 0.5-1 per cent may be 
obtained. This is due to the fact that nitrous acid does not react 
instantaneously with the permanganate.
More accurate results may be secured by adding the nitrite to an acidified 
solution in which permanganate is present in excess ( the tip of the 
pipette containing the nitrite solution should be below the surface of the 
liquid during the addition ), and back titrating the potassium permanganate with 
a solution of ferrous ammonium sulphate which has recently been compared with 
the permanganate solution.
For practice in this determination, it may be determine the purity of commercial 
potassium nitrite.
Safety Precautions
The sample must be taken as the applicable ASTM methods D 
 3370-76.
The sample must be kept away from exposure to direct 
 sunlight.
Acids such 
 as sulfuric acid and others are dangerous, so you have to wear breathing mask.
Keep these 
 acids closed. Do not get it in the eyes, on the skin, or on clothing. Do not 
 breathe them, use only in a hood.
Tools and Equipment
Apparatus
Pipets- Since this analysis depends on the amount of KMnO4 
consumed, it is imperative that pipets for delivering the potassium permanganate 
standard solution be calibrated and cleaned for maximum precision.
Volumetric Flasks.
Heater.
Reagents
Potassium Permanganate Standard Solution ( 0.1 N ).
Conc. Sulphuric Acid.
Commercial Potassium Nitrite.
Work To be Carried Out
Procedure
Weigh out accurately about 1.1 g. of 
commercial potassium nitrite, dissolve it in cold water, and dilute to 250 
ml. in a volumetric flask. Shake well.
Measure out 5 ml. of standard 0.1N-potassium permanganate into a 100-ml. flask, add 2.26 ml. conc. sulfuric 
acid, and heat to 40C.
Place the nitrite solution in the burette, and add 
it slowly and with constant stirring until the permanganate solution is just 
decolorised, better results are attained by allowing the tip of the burette to 
dip under the surface of the diluted permanganate solution.
Towards the end of the reaction is sluggish, so 
that the nitrite solution must be added very slowly.
Repeat the titration with two other 25 ml. portions 
of the permanganate solution.

0.02300 g. NO2 ≡ 0.04256 g. KNO2
